gloss: dead leaves; dry leaves; fallen leaves

definitions.gloss: dead leaves; dry leaves; fallen leaves
definitions.explanation: Leaves that have dried up and fallen from trees or plants, especially in autumn and winter. A common seasonal image in literature and everyday language.

examples.japanese: {枯|か}れ{葉|は}が{舞|ま}っている。
examples.english: Dead leaves are swirling in the air.

examples.japanese: {道|みち}に{枯|か}れ{葉|は}がたくさん{落|お}ちていた。
examples.english: There were lots of dead leaves on the road.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}の{枯|か}れ{葉|は}を{集|あつ}めて{焚|た}き{火|び}をした。
examples.english: I gathered the dead leaves in the yard and made a bonfire.

notes:
An evocative seasonal word strongly associated with late autumn and winter. In Japanese poetry and literature, {枯|か}れ{葉|は} conveys transience, loneliness, and the passing of time. In everyday use, it simply refers to dried, fallen leaves.

FORMS:
{枯|か}れ (withered, dried) + {葉|は} (leaf)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {枯|か}れ{葉|は}が{舞|ま}う: dead leaves dance in the wind
- {枯|か}れ{葉|は}を{踏|ふ}む: to step on dry leaves
- {枯|か}れ{葉|は}を{集|あつ}める: to gather fallen leaves
- {枯|か}れ{葉|は}の{山|やま}: a pile of dead leaves

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {落|お}ち{葉|ば}: fallen leaves — emphasizes the act of having fallen; broader and includes fresh leaves that have just dropped
- {紅葉|もみじ}: autumn leaves — focuses on colorful leaves still on trees or freshly fallen, with a positive aesthetic nuance
- {落葉|らくよう}: leaf fall, defoliation — more formal/botanical term for the process of leaves falling
